description: A rank-2 weight whose innermost dimension is rounded UP to a multiple of 16 elements, so every row starts on an aligned boundary. Row-major otherwise; the fill elements are zero and mean nothing.
name: torch.stride-padding-16
provenance: THE ALIGNMENT IS IN THE NAME BECAUSE IT IS IN THE MAP. `stride-padding` is a family, not a layout: padding to 16 and padding to 8 are two different arrangements of the same tensor, and one name for two maps is exactly the collision the digest exists to prevent. A different alignment is a different record (`stride-padding-8@1`), and its provenance owes the kernel that asked for it.

16 is the alignment `cozy.nvfp4-flat@1` already records as the kernel's own: torch's fp4 `scaled_mm` needs packed K/2 % 16, which is `_K_ALIGN`/`_N_ALIGN` in python-gen-worker `src/gen_worker/models/w4a4.py`. This record is the arrangement that satisfies it for a tensor whose logical inner dim does not.

THE FIRST PADDED RECORD IN THE CLASS, and it is why the auto-ratification verifier checks INJECTIVITY and round-trip-on-the-image rather than bijection: the destination is larger than the source, so applying the map and then its inverse must return the source bytes exactly while the fill bytes stay zero and unread.
